conventions.form: EndpointOK (formal/lean/Formal/Core/Substrate/CornerNat.lean): for every data path P and every request path Q of a form, sum over P of each arc's upper delay + margin_ps <= sum over Q of each arc's lower delay, both measured from the form's common `launch` event. With a corner model this is EndpointOK kappa (path P) (path Q) (margin + |P| + |Q|) (bundle_band, one ps of rounding per arc); with fixed intervals it is shard C's 10a race check.
conventions.combine: 'all': every form must hold (default). 'any': the obligation holds if one form holds (RT1, RT1b: race OR structural).
conventions.names: cell-relative: `<lut instance>.<logical pin>` (I0..I5, O5, O6); `<u>.<pin>@pip` is the site-pin input of that LUT pin. The checker maps logical pins to the physical A1..A6 the router chose (routed JSON X_ORIG_PORT_A<k> / ROUTING sitewire, or FASM). `{I0|I1}` = max (data side) or min (request side) over those pins. Bracketed indices (ctl[i], lat[b]) are pipe stages.

arc_kinds.lut_arc: cell IOPATH from a logical input pin to an output (prjxray per pin/output: O6 45/124 flat over pins; O5 from I0/I1 44/152, from I2 42/150; FAST_MIN/SLOW_MAX ps). nextpnr SDF: flat 124.
arc_kinds.site_pin: input site-pin buffer of the physical LUT pin, SP[pin]; prjxray tile_type_CLBL{L,M}_{L,R}.json (fast_min, fast_max, slow_min, slow_max) ps: A1 (172,214,416,516), A2 (170,212,409,507), A3 (107,133,278,344), A4 (86,107,229,284), A5 (33,42,91,112), A6 (2,2,4,5); SLICEM A1 up to 531, D1 540. nextpnr SDF: flat 25 ps (then subtract 25 from INTERCONNECT if it includes the site pip; check on one SDF).
arc_kinds.wire: routed INTERCONNECT from a driver output to a sink pin, excluding the site pin (prjxray pips + Elmore RC, or SDF band).
arc_kinds.feedback_wire: routed wire from a LUT's output back to its own input pin (the loop wire; tighten.loop_wire).
arc_kinds.line: traversal of a bd_delay line (or request/DACK line) for one edge along a named path (chain/ripple/tap/fastest); expands to wire + LUT arcs per hop.
arc_kinds.env: a segment outside the cell (neighbour response, server, sender, protocol latency); resolved by the checker by walking the routed netlist when it is inside the design, else an environment hypothesis.
arc_kinds.cell_param: datasheet / chipdb constant (BRAM tSU, tHD, tCO, tPWH).

conventions.lean_sym: the symbol the arc instantiates in the cited Lean statement (dlmax, dwmax, wfa1, ...).
conventions.site_pins: `needed` = the obligation's exact form contains per-pin site delays; `roles` = which logical pin roles and on which side. The SDF cannot see them (flat 25 ps).
conventions.corner_rule: prjxray's two IOPATH triples are FAST and SLOW corners, NOT rise and fall (ArbCorners.prj_is_mix; prjxray makesdf.py:63). NEVER take a rise arc from FAST and a fall arc from SLOW. Modes: '1C' = both sides from one column, checked at FAST_MIN and at SLOW_MAX (or EndpointOK with kappa over a shared corner); 'box' = every hi at SLOW_MAX and every lo at FAST_MIN independently (always sound, pessimistic); '1C_both_corners_required' = a SLOW_MAX-only check is NOT enough (RT1b). A SLOW_MAX-only margin needs the guard As - Af/k (fast_neg_iff; As - Af if k <= 1, guard_universal). Rise = fall within a column (H_RF_ASYM unmeasured). Bj5 (ConstraintsKappa, Bk2): '1C' as two columns is GenOK at kappa = 0 and unsound for kappa > 0 (one_corner_unsound_with_kappa); 'box' is sound only in the independent-box model (every delay in [FAST_MIN, SLOW_MAX], H_DELAY_BOX), not in A's kappa model (box_unsound_with_kappa); a SLOW_MAX-only check is unsound in A's model even at kappa = 0 (slow_only_unsound); the As - Af/k guard is the H_WIRE_RATIO model's. See conventions.kappa.
conventions.status: 'proved' = every cited sufficient theorem exists in a tracked file; 'unproved' = the inequality is not a Lean statement (extrapolated, physical reading of an untimed result, or no theorem).
conventions.exactness: sufficient | sufficient+necessary (a counter-trace shows the condition cannot be dropped) | sufficient+necessary_at_boundary/instance (tight on a concrete trace, not a general iff) | exact (iff; see exact_scope / exact_under when present) | not_necessary (sufficient, but a theorem shows the condition is not needed; see `replacement`) | sufficient+necessary_untimed (S/N in an untimed model; the delay inequality is its physical reading) | untimed_schedule | hypothesis (a named assumption the cell theorems use, not derived) | sufficient_by_arithmetic | see_refers_to | partial (status stays 'unproved': a weaker statement than the entry is proved; exactness_note says what is missing) | unproved.
conventions.rule_verdicts: exact | conservative | missing_term (rule weaker; `missing` names the term) | exact_arcs_missing_site_pins | conservative_arcs_missing_site_pins | rule_is_the_check | different_condition | none (no rule checks it) | uncheckable_statically.
conventions.check_scope: static_route (route + prjxray only) | route_plus_env (needs a neighbour or environment latency; static when the neighbour is in the design) | environment | protocol | structural | not_static.
conventions.exact_scope: optional text: which forms or parts of an 'exact' entry are exact; the rest of the entry is sufficient only (e.g. bdc_muxn.s_setup: decode form exact, data LUT5 form sufficient).
conventions.necessity_scope: optional text: where the necessity half of an entry's exactness holds (a consumer kind, or a subset of its forms).
conventions.informational: true: the entry is implied by the entries in refers_to; a checker that evaluates those need not evaluate it.
conventions.replacement: for exactness 'not_necessary': the named hypothesis (hypotheses_not_inequalities) or the constraint id that is the needed condition in its place (bd_merge.uxa_feedback / uxa_req_latency -> bd_merge.uxa_loop; kept for traceability, a checker evaluates the replacement).
conventions.lean_roles: role of each citation. 'exact': the theorem's statement is an iff (contains '↔'; the validator checks this) for the entry's inequality or a named part of it (see exact_scope). 'exact_inner': an iff for a race, sub-case or special case INSIDE the entry (e.g. CElemStrict's own-feedback race behind the strict +1 of a composed entry, or the one-node bd_ctree case); it does not make the entry exact. 'exact_formula': a closed-form equality for a quantity (e.g. an overlap duration), not an iff. Other roles: sufficient, necessary, counter_trace, non_vacuity, instance, lemma, definition, context, not_necessary*, redundancy, ... (as named). 'counter_run': a theorem that an explicit run satisfies the model (Run / CSide / a line) for all t, used by a counter_trace; 'numbers': a decided arithmetic fact about a counter-run (which field it violates by how much). A 'necessary at the boundary' refutation (a theorem of the form NOT Claim(weakened by 1)) is cited as counter_trace, never as exact.
conventions.exact_under: optional list of named side conditions: the entry's 'exact' holds only under them; outside them it is sufficient only.
conventions.strictness: Bs (formal/notes/B-celem-strict.md, Formal/Cells/CElemStrict.lean): in the per-pin Kleene mux-tree model (H_TREE, H_MUX_KLEENE: a moving select reads X on [s, s + wa), wa >= 1 tick; H_FB_PURE) the own-feedback race is clean iff dlmax + dwmax + wa <= dlmin + E (env_latency_iff), so with the grid minimum wa = 1 ps every own-feedback race entry reads L + 1 <= R (env_latency_strict; at equality bd_c2 reads X, boundary_x) and every held width >= Dmax + 1. Entries carrying `strict` have margin_ps raised by 1 on the forms it lists; their earlier '<=' theorems are proved with instantaneous selects (wa = 0, env_latency_atomic) and remain sufficient. The 1 ps is the model's minimum, NOT a measured slew: the physical margin is the departing select's X width (with SDF 50% arrival times about half the sum of the two select slews), which nothing here measures. `strict_pending` marks input-against-input orders where the same mechanism may apply but has not been checked; they stay '<='. Bj5: the select setup/hold rows of bd_steer, bd_mux and bdc_muxn are strict on KleeneBox's backing (steer_strict_K, join_strict_K, muxn_edges_K at w = 1): in binary-edge times under H_KLEENE_LUT + H_X_UNIFORM they are exact WITH the +1; in definite-window times the '<=' form is exact. bd_ctree.node_loop and bd_merge.uxa_loop moved from strict to strict_pending: their iffs (tree_box_exact, uxa_box_exact) are binary '<=' and the +1 was not re-proved for them (audit P8). An entry labelled exact that carries `strict` must cite as 'exact' an iff that covers the +1 form (validator: STRICT_IFFS).
conventions.guards_in_rules: tighten.py A, D, F, H, I, K, L add req_guard = max(0.2 t, 200 ps); skew.py (E) and arb_fork.py (J) use 0.772 early / 1.155 late (GUARD_LO/GUARD_HI).
conventions.tcheck_mapping: for one form: node 0 = launch; each path is a chain of 10a arcs [lo, hi] from node 0; data = the end nodes of the data paths; req = one node joined by the request paths' ends (the earliest change of any); setup = margin_ps. tcheck's PASS is then `verdict_sound` (every data change precedes every request change by setup). A shared arc on both sides (same element, as in setup_pulse) is CPPR-pessimistic under FixedRun (C-10a corr).
conventions.binds_at: optional (reset-width rows): where in gcd_hw the width condition binds, from Brst (ResetGcdVec) and Bfw (ResetGcdVec2): reset_vector = cells at a hold vector of the reset vector rho (gcd_vec_census, exact there by gcd_hold_exact); per_cell_model = cells that bind in the per-cell two-phase model (adds newHoldL); network = cells left in Rst2's GMW network under its global rst hold (gcd_reset_vec_of_net). `lean` names citations of the entry's own `lean` list (the validator checks this and the counts).
conventions.kappa: corner.kappa on every 1C / 1C_both_corners_required row: the form under A's corner model (hypotheses_not_inequalities 'H_SHARED_CORNER / H_SCATTER (kappa)'). Check: GenOK at both endpoints, unrounded (sound: allOK_of_gen; exact only under H_DISJ + H_DIV: allOK_iff_gen; otherwise sandwich). kappa is UNMEASURED on the current toolchain, so every kappa verdict is conditional. corner.kappa.results (arbiter rows) quotes OnNetlistArbKappa / OnGcdArbKappa: kappa* is a proved SAFE bound; the unsafe side is proved only from a larger kappa (link_arb: kappa* + 6/(E+L), gap not decided; gcd_hw: kappa_u <= kappa* + 1.8e-5, arc-form level only). Per-pair thresholds are NOT exact (audit row 18).
conventions.hypotheses: optional list on an entry (Bj5): the named model hypotheses its cited theorems take (e.g. H_KLEENE_LUT, H_X_UNIFORM, H_PIN_FIFO, the scope Wf of LinkExact). Rows touched before Bj5 carry them in exactness_note prose instead.

constraints.exactness_note: exact for fixed transport delays: every runt 0 < w < dl+dw oscillates for ever (counter_trace). STRICT (Bs): own-feedback race, L <= R is now L + 1 <= R (margin_ps + 1 on forms [0], held width >= Dmax + 1); the cited '<=' theorems are proved with instantaneous selects (H_ATOMIC_LUT / zero-width windows) and stay sufficient for the strict form. See conventions.strictness.

rule.detail: UNCHECKED as such; inside a four-phase run it is implied by the env_latency entry (c2_four_phase derives c(k+1) >= c k + Dmax).

corner.rule: evaluate both sides in the SAME prjxray column, once at FAST_MIN and once at SLOW_MAX (H_ONE_CORNER): this is GenOK at kappa = 0, unsound in A's model for kappa > 0 (ConstraintsKappa.one_corner_unsound_with_kappa); with kappa use GenOK at both endpoints (corner.kappa). box (every hi at SLOW_MAX, every lo at FAST_MIN) is sound only when every delay lies in [FAST_MIN, SLOW_MAX] (H_DELAY_BOX), NOT in A's kappa model for kappa > 0 (box_unsound_with_kappa; with kappa: (1+kappa)S vs (1-kappa)F). A SLOW_MAX-only check is unsound in A's model even at kappa = 0 (slow_only_unsound); the guard As - Af/k (ArbCorners.fast_neg_iff) belongs to the H_WIRE_RATIO model only. Never rise=FAST / fall=SLOW.

kappa.check: GenOK at the FAST and SLOW endpoints, unrounded: (1+kappa)*sum_P ep + a <= (1-kappa)*sum_Q ep + b, a/b the data-side / request-side constants (ConstraintsKappa.allOK_of_gen: sound; allOK_iff_gen: exact under H_DISJ + H_DIV; sandwich otherwise). kappa = 0 is the one-column check.

constraints.exactness_note: Bmx (formal/notes/B-lib-gap-mux.md): exact (iff) per join over the delay box with PER-PIN reads of all four live pins (x/y_req I0, ctl_req I1, s I2, own feedback I3; read maps need not be monotone), s adversarial outside [S0,S1), the client request arbitrary. The request and feedback windows drop out of the condition (they only shape the failure: latched wrong-branch token if the bad window outlasts the loop, else a recirculating runt). Necessity per join: unselected join with the other client's request waiting; selected join with its request waiting (setup) or already fallen (hold). Box necessity assumes pin delays independent; under a correlated corner model use join_pin_exact per realisation. O6 LUT arcs are flat over pins in prjxray, so the per-pin content is the site pins SP[I1], SP[I2]. Supersedes the window-model sufficient form (ConstraintsMux.*_unsel_low_timed) for this obligation. Not covered: bdc_muxn (other INITs; its rows are bdc_muxn.s_setup / s_hold), the ctl_req fork as a C rule K obligation, the source of S0/S1, mid-rail select (H_KLEENE_LUT). STRICT (Bkx, KleeneBox): with K3 traces on EVERY pin (request, ctl_req, select / index bits, feedback) and the real INITs through lutK (H_KLEENE_LUT: the exact, hazard-free ternary extension of the INIT, i.e. the OPTIMISTIC LUT model; its silicon fidelity is unverified, audit P8), two coordinate systems: (a) DEFINITE-WINDOW times (the windows on which each pin is definite): the condition is the binary one, '<=', and exact (K3 safety <-> binary safety); (b) BINARY-EDGE times under H_X_UNIFORM (every edge X on [T - a, T + c), the SAME split on every edge, w = a + c): every setup and hold gains +w, exact; at w = 1 tick (the grid minimum, NOT a measured slew) strict. The row's forms are in (b) with w = 1 (margin_ps + 1). With unequal splits per edge only (a) applies. Not covered: the X width, mid-rail selects beyond H_KLEENE_LUT, correlated corners.

constraints.exactness_note: Bmx (formal/notes/B-lib-gap-mux.md): exact (iff) per join over the delay box with PER-PIN reads of all four live pins (x/y_req I0, ctl_req I1, s I2, own feedback I3; read maps need not be monotone), s adversarial outside [S0,S1), the client request arbitrary. The request and feedback windows drop out of the condition (they only shape the failure: latched wrong-branch token if the bad window outlasts the loop, else a recirculating runt). Necessity per join: unselected join with the other client's request waiting; selected join with its request waiting (setup) or already fallen (hold). Box necessity assumes pin delays independent; under a correlated corner model use join_pin_exact per realisation. O6 LUT arcs are flat over pins in prjxray, so the per-pin content is the site pins SP[I1], SP[I2]. Supersedes the window-model sufficient form (ConstraintsMux.*_unsel_low_timed) for this obligation. Not covered: bdc_muxn (other INITs; its rows are bdc_muxn.s_setup / s_hold), the ctl_req fork as a C rule K obligation, the source of S0/S1, mid-rail select (H_KLEENE_LUT). STRICT (Bkx, KleeneBox): with K3 traces on EVERY pin (request, ctl_req, select / index bits, feedback) and the real INITs through lutK (H_KLEENE_LUT: the exact, hazard-free ternary extension of the INIT, i.e. the OPTIMISTIC LUT model; its silicon fidelity is unverified, audit P8), two coordinate systems: (a) DEFINITE-WINDOW times (the windows on which each pin is definite): the condition is the binary one, '<=', and exact (K3 safety <-> binary safety); (b) BINARY-EDGE times under H_X_UNIFORM (every edge X on [T - a, T + c), the SAME split on every edge, w = a + c): every setup and hold gains +w, exact; at w = 1 tick (the grid minimum, NOT a measured slew) strict. The row's forms are in (b) with w = 1 (margin_ps + 1). With unequal splits per edge only (a) applies. Not covered: the X width, mid-rail selects beyond H_KLEENE_LUT, correlated corners.

Needed for c2n/c2n_set even with inputs at reset values; for c2/c3/c4/uj0/uj1 NOT needed once every input reads 0 (c2_inputs0_selfreset). FORM FIXED (Bj2): the earlier form charged the I_rst arc only on the data side, so in BOX mode it was short by (arc hi - arc lo - 1) per pin (json_box_gap, json_box_gap_fails: W = 917 passed the form, the exact box needs 995); it was sound only in 1C. The form now has the I_rst arc lo on the request side and the feedback-pin arc hi on the data side, as bd_latch_rst.reset form 0, which is the exact box condition plus the strict +1. Arbiter ustate not covered. Earlier: P6 / Rst: sufficient; the per-cell form of bd_c*.reset_width, now with a general bd_c2n theorem. Necessity not shown separately (same loop as pulse_width). Rst/Rst2: no route, so no form is evaluated. ResetGcd's results are about the ELABORATED RTL control netlist of gcd_hw (bdc default DELAY_* sizes, gcd_rig CMPD = 16; 3322 nodes, real INITs and pin lists, Verilog -> Lean by an unverified generator cross-checked against yosys by WL colour refinement), not the synthesized or routed netlist. The GMW network theorems are in model steps (D = LUT bound, W = wire bound); the per-cell timed lemmas are window channels; the two are not one theorem. STRICT (Bs): own-feedback race, L <= R is now L + 1 <= R (margin_ps + 1 on forms [0]); the cited '<=' theorems are proved with instantaneous selects (H_ATOMIC_LUT / zero-width windows) and stay sufficient for the strict form. See conventions.strictness. Bj4 (binds_at; Brst / Bfw): in gcd_hw the width binds at 195 hold-vector cells at the reset vector (gcd_vec_census; exact there, gcd_hold_exact, which also covers the 9 arbiter ustate O6 at their real LUT), at up to 206 in the per-cell model (newHoldL, newHold_exact) and at none in the GMW network under Rst2's global hold (gcd_reset_vec_of_net).

Cell level: an input edge that reaches a reset cell while its rst is still read high and then stays is processed exactly as if it arrived at release (early_request_ok, numbers early_request_numbers). The exact cell-level requirement is H_NO_RETURN: an input pulse that completes while rst is read high is lost (returned_pulse_lost). Design level: ResetGcdWave.gcd_wave_settled proves H_NO_RETURN for the reset-release window on gcd_hw's control network for EVERY rst waveform (any skew, glitches, re-assertion), so this skew bound is not needed there; the residual is H_RST_BEFORE_LOOP (rst final W < 34 GMW steps before the loop is first requested: gcd_loop_late, rst_reads_low). Kept as a sufficient form only; see hypotheses_not_inequalities H_NO_RETURN. Earlier: P6 / Rst2: gcd_release_quiet (kernel-checked on the imported gcd_hw network) makes release skew UNNECESSARY for 'nothing moves before a frontier link fires': it holds for every skew. What H_RST_SKEW still buys is the step after: a frontier fires while some cell's rst is still high, and that cell could miss a complete input pulse (H_NO_RETURN, argued, not proved). So this form is only sufficient, and a checker need evaluate it only for first-wave cells; for the 1-LUT paths to fork ack trees (likely to fail) the race lemmas make it harmless. Rst/Rst2: no route, so no form is evaluated. ResetGcd's results are about the ELABORATED RTL control netlist of gcd_hw (bdc default DELAY_* sizes, gcd_rig CMPD = 16; 3322 nodes, real INITs and pin lists, Verilog -> Lean by an unverified generator cross-checked against yosys by WL colour refinement), not the synthesized or routed netlist. The GMW network theorems are in model steps (D = LUT bound, W = wire bound); the per-cell timed lemmas are window channels; the two are not one theorem.

CAVEAT (Bfd, B-fork-data.md section 3): Cm2's consumer is edge-sampling (index settled su before Zr), and the necessity above holds only at such a consumer. Every index consumer in gcd_hw is a Muller bd_link/bd_pipe behind the _f fork, which closes a whole handshake after Zr: the counter-traces show a stale index at the request edge, not a stale latched value. constraints.exact_scope: iff relative to LinkExact's Spec (window-token node + capture), ONLY inside the scope Wf and Split. Wf holds conditions that are NOT in the conjunction: ordered windows (0 <= lo <= hi for every pin, 1 <= Qlo, 1 <= Flo, W <= W1, Ra <= Ra1 <= Fa <= Fa1, Rb <= Rb1 <= Fb <= Fb1), H_RST_EARLY (W1 + Rhi < Ra + Alo: rst surely read low before req can be read moved), H_RST_EARLY_ACK (W1 + Rhi < Rb + Blo, the same for ack), H_ACK_ORDER (V1 <= Fb + Blo; implied by H_RACE_DN). Split (H_REL_SPLIT, Fa + Alo != Rb + Blo) is needed only for the necessity of H_RACE_UP: at the release tie that necessity is NOT decided. Binary '<=' in definite-window times; strict in binary-edge times (strict_edges). Data path: the en = c variant (not BD_LINK_DC). NOT covered: closed loop, more than one token, a W-bit bus as one theorem, the input port, correlated corners (pins independent in the box).
constraints.exactness_note: Blink (formal/notes/B-link-exact.md, LinkExact.lean): all seven pins (req, ack, own feedback, rst, data, enable, latch loop) read through their own NON-monotone windows (H_CTL_READ / H_PIN_READ, real INITs in Kleene semantics), power-up arbitrary, environment and data arbitrary (X included) outside their definite windows (H_ENV, one token, open loop). Finding: no cross-cell condition (no_cross); the coupling is substitution only: the controller's req-pin spread Ahi - Alo enters the latch's setup_pulse budget, the latch hold window closes at the controller's slow reads V1, and latch hold rests on the controller's fall race. Audit P8: CONFIRMED (iff, both sides inhabited in scope).

cells: every reset cell whose rst is still high when a frontier link fires
hypotheses_not_inequalities.statement: no input of a cell still held in reset rises AND returns before the cell's rst releases (a lost event). Cell level (Bsx, NecessityReset): this is the exact requirement: a pulse that completes while rst is read high is lost (returned_pulse_lost), while an edge that arrives early and stays is processed as if it arrived at release (early_request_ok), so 'released before the first request' (H_RST_EARLY, design.rst_release_skew) is sufficient, not necessary. Design level (Rst3, ResetGcdWave): PROVED for the reset-release window on gcd_hw's elaborated control network: for every rst waveform on (S, F] (any per-pin skew, glitches, re-assertion) every control node is at the same state sigB from F + 34(D+W+1) until the first loop request (gcd_wave_settled, from gcd_first_wave; model steps D = LUT bound, W = wire bound). Residual: H_RST_BEFORE_LOOP, rst final before the loop is first requested, which holds with a clean rst edge when W < 34 steps (gcd_clean_release, gcd_loop_late, rst_reads_low). The loop phases (after the first steer request) are not covered.

hypotheses_not_inequalities.statement: H_KLEENE_LUT: a LUT output is lutK of its K3 pin reads (Core's mux tree with mux(X, a, b) = a if a = b else X), which is the exact ternary closure of the INIT over all Boolean completions (audit P8 re-checked it on 729 vectors for 6 INITs): the hazard-free, OPTIMISTIC LUT model (e.g. C2(1,1,X) = 1), pin-order independent. H_X_UNIFORM: every binary edge T carries an X window [T - a, T + c) with the SAME split on every edge (w = a + c). w = 1 tick is the grid minimum, not a measured slew.
